discovery: Programmable Rydberg-atom arrays for quantum simulation and quantum computation

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

nominees.name: Antoine Browaeys
nominees.affiliation: Institut d'Optique, CNRS, Université Paris-Saclay, France

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum information
motivation: Individually trapped neutral atoms coupled through the Rydberg blockade have become one of the most powerful platforms for controlling many-body quantum systems. Zoller, with co-workers, proposed the Rydberg blockade as a mechanism for fast entangling gates between neutral atoms and laid much of the theoretical groundwork for quantum simulation with cold atoms. Browaeys pioneered the experimental observation of the blockade between two single atoms and built reconfigurable optical-tweezer arrays that realise programmable quantum spin models. Lukin co-proposed the blockade and dipole-blockade ideas, and his group scaled atom arrays to hundreds of qubits. They observed quantum phase transitions, many-body scars and topological spin liquids, and demonstrated logical qubits with error-detected and error-corrected circuits. Together these works turned atomic physics into a scalable, programmable quantum machine. They opened new regimes of many-body physics and set a decisive path towards fault-tolerant quantum computation.
